changes: Fixes DOWN and UP sustaining themselves with FDBK near 127 after the input stops (octabam issue 825). You no longer need to keep FDBK at 120 or below.
Upstream changed the module: Bryan T lowered SHIFT's feedback limit, so every FDBK setting feeds back a little less than in 0.1.0. RING, SRR, BRR, LPF and the knobs are unchanged.
Known issue: four LOFI2 in SHIFT on T5-T8 with FX1 in use locked up an MKII (octabam issue 850). Over USB the base allows two per DSP core; in card builds avoid four on one core.
Known issue: a very faint SHIFT residue remains after the input stops, and reloads, power cycles and several instances are not yet tested on hardware with 0.1.1.
First Modwerk import of Bryan T's LOFI2 from octabam: ring modulator or stereo frequency shifter (MODE RING / DOWN / UP), then sample-rate and bit reduction and a high-shelf cut.
Upstream code is unchanged, including the author's faster version and his SHIFT fix that suppresses the unwanted sideband in DOWN and UP much better.
Modwerk repackaging: a different effect ID, so octabam LOFI2 projects don't select it, and RNGE as the range name. Card builds give up two stock reverbs and can't include Analog BD.
Over USB the beta base loads LOFI2 into FX1 or FX2; two fit on one DSP core and a third is refused (DSP FULL). The self-test failed with LOFI2 plus five other modules.
Known issue: with RNGE HIGH, FREQ about 60 to 76 and FDBK 124 or more, SHIFT keeps sounding after the input stops; keep FDBK at 120 or below there (octabam issue 825).
